roasterArchitectures.description: Continuous industrial roasting drum engineered for large-scale coffee, cocoa, and grain processing. Features a perforated internal spiral flight auger that conveys product continuously through counter-flow heated combustion gas. Forced-draft modulating gas burner maintains tight excess air ratios, while pneumatic chaff ducting transports combustible silver skins to an outdoor spark-quenched cyclone collector fitted with certified explosion rupture panels.

roasterArchitectures.description: Commercial batch roasting system for specialty coffee, malted brewing grains, and seeds. Utilizes a solid double-wall cast-iron drum with indirect hot-air convection. An auxiliary thermal afterburner oxidizes volatile organic compounds (VOCs), smoke aldehydes, and residual carbon monoxide before atmospheric release, while chaff is separated in an external cyclone with an automated rotary lock to prevent ember backdraft.

roasterArchitectures.description: Mid-sized artisan coffee and nut drum roaster with direct open gas flame impingement on a rotating steel drum. Roaster exhaust air and combustible chaff skins are pulled through a compact indoor cyclone collector. Susceptible to air suction loss, chaff smoldering, and combustion gas backdraft when exhaust flues accumulate carbonized chaff deposits or during sudden barometric inversion.

roasterArchitectures.classification: Critical Non-Compliant Installation (Severe Chaff Dust Deflagration & Deadly CO Infiltration Hazard)

roasterArchitectures.chaffHandling: Uninsulated Ductwork with Heavy Creosote Caking and Overfilled Indoor Metal Dust Bin
roasterArchitectures.flueMonitoring: Inoperative Flue Damper with Zero Gas Monitoring (Direct CO Infiltration into Roastery Floor)
roasterArchitectures.description: Aging roasting plant lacking modern NFPA 61/86 safety devices. Flue ducting has not been de-chaffed or hydro-cleaned, causing low air velocity (<10 m/s) below chaff saltation thresholds. Chaff settles inside horizontal duct elbows, where contact with high-temperature flue sparks induces glowing ember smoldering. Insufficient burner draft drives incomplete combustion with flue gas carbon monoxide levels exceeding 600 ppm.

processingGrains.name: Green Arabica & Robusta Coffee Beans (Exothermic Crack, Heavy Silver Skin, Pyrolysis Gases)
processingGrains.description: During roasting, green coffee beans undergo endothermic moisture loss followed by violent exothermic pyrolysis ('first crack' at ~200°C and 'second crack' at ~225°C). The papery silver skin (epiderm) detaches as lightweight chaff flakes. Rapid cellular decomposition off-gasses carbon monoxide, carbon dioxide, furans, and volatile hydrocarbons. Chaff particles exhibit high surface area and can deflagrate violently when suspended in hot exhaust air.

processingGrains.name: Fermented & Dried Raw Cocoa Beans (High Fat Content, Acetic Acid Vapor, Flake Chaff)
processingGrains.description: Cocoa beans are roasted at lower temperatures (130°C to 155°C) to develop chocolate flavor precursors while shedding fibrous husk shells. Volatilized acetic acid and fat droplets deposit on cyclone walls, creating tacky residues that trap fine husk dust. While cocoa shell dust has a lower deflagration index than grain chaff, oily deposits are prone to smoldering autoignition if left in heated collectors.

processingGrains.name: Malted Brewing Barley & Specialty Grains (Micro-Fine Chaff Dust, High Starch Combustibility)
processingGrains.description: Malted barley roasted for dark stouts and porter malts sheds dry awns and husks that shatter into sub-60-micron airborne organic dust. Malt dust exhibits very low minimum ignition energy (MIE < 25 mJ) and a high deflagration severity index (Kst > 200 bar·m/s). Sparks from direct burner flames entering the malt dust stream can trigger explosive primary and secondary duct deflagrations.

processingGrains.name: Shelled Peanuts & Tree Nuts (Low Chaff, High Oil Aerosol, Smoldering Ember Spontaneous Fire)
processingGrains.description: Nuts release minimal thin skin dust compared to grain chaff, but high lipid content (45% to 55% fat) generates volatilized oil smoke aerosol. Liquid grease droplets condense on exhaust duct surfaces, forming combustible varnish. Settled nut debris in uncleaned roaster bottoms undergoes spontaneous exothermic autoignition, producing smoldering embers that emit dense carbon monoxide.

scientificFormulas.coCombustion: CO_flue = k_co / (lambda - 0.90)^1.85, where lambda is excess air ratio (lambda < 1.0 triggers exponential CO rise)
scientificFormulas.chaffConcentration: C_chaff = (M_dot_feed * Y_chaff) / Q_duct (g/m3), compared to MEC (40-65 g/m3)
scientificFormulas.deflagrationSeverity: K_st = (dP/dt)_max * V^(1/3) (bar*m/s), classified St 1 (0-200) or St 2 (201-300)
scientificFormulas.saltationVelocity: V_salt = 1.25 * sqrt(g * D_duct * (rho_chaff / rho_air)) (m/s), typically 14-16 m/s required to prevent settling
